title: Virtual DOM
body:
A lightweight tree of plain JavaScript objects describing what the UI *should* look like. It is not a browser feature — it lives entirely in the JS engine, in library code such as [[React]]. When state changes, the library builds a new virtual tree, compares it to the previous one, and works out the minimum set of real [[DOM]] operations required.

In the stage-set analogy: rather than walking onto the stage yourself every time you want something moved, you hand the stagehand a marked-up blueprint and let them figure out the smallest set of changes. The win isn't that diffing is free — it isn't — it's that touching the real DOM is expensive ([[Reflow]], [[Repaint]]) and object comparison in memory is cheap, plus updates get batched instead of applied one at a time. See [[Reconciliation]].
